title: Predictive Disk / Volume Exhaustion
exclusions: Does not replace enterprise SIEM correlation for unrelated threat classes. Does not constitute legal, regulatory, or executive attestation for 'Predictive Disk / Volume Exhaustion'. Does not cover entities explicitly scoped out in operational_exceptions.csv. Pair with sibling UCs in the same subcategory when the SPL surface alone cannot prove control effectiveness (see prerequisiteUseCases on UC-20.1.9).
evidence: Saved search uc_20_1_9_predictive_disk_volume_exhaustion, dashboard panel tied to this UC, weekly CSV export archived to index=evidence with change-ticket reference, and git-tracked lookup baselines referenced in the search.

controlTest.positiveScenario: On a lab host or staging index, ingest sample events that satisfy all SPL filters for 'Predictive Disk / Volume Exhaustion'. Run the saved search manually and confirm at least one result row with populated severity or metric fields. Verify the alert action fires within one schedule interval and the output matches the dashboard table projection for UC-20.1.9.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest a control batch where threshold fields remain within normal bounds (for example compliant configuration values, timestamps outside the monitoring window, or entities listed in operational_exceptions.csv). dataSources: df/disk usage data (any sourcetype with UsePct and filesystem), SNMP storage MIBs Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
spl:
index=infrastructure (sourcetype="df" OR sourcetype="disk")
| eval UsePct=coalesce(UsePct, pctUsed, 'Percent_Used')
| eval filesystem=coalesce(filesystem, mount, instance)
| where isnotnull(UsePct) AND isnotnull(filesystem)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats latest(UsePct) as used_pct by filesystem, host, _time
| timechart span=1d latest(used_pct) as used_pct by filesystem, host
| predict used_pct as predicted_pct algorithm=LLP5 future_timespan=90
| eval risk_30d=if('predicted_pct+30d'>85, "At Risk", "OK")
| eval risk_90d=if('predicted_pct+90d'>95, "Critical", "OK")
| where risk_30d="At Risk" OR risk_90d="Critical"
| table _time, filesystem, host, used_pct, 'predicted_pct+30d', 'predicted_pct+90d', risk_30d, risk_90d
description: Time-to-full forecast using linear regression on disk usage data enables proactive capacity planning. Running out of disk space causes application outages, failed backups, and data loss. Predicting exhaustion dates allows teams to provision storage or archive data before hitting critical thresholds.
value: Operations and leadership rely on 'Predictive Disk / Volume Exhaustion' to catch regressions before they become customer-visible outages or audit findings. Early signal reduces mean time to repair, avoids duplicate manual log review, and preserves evidence for post-incident review without waiting for a user-reported ticket.
implementation: Collect disk usage metrics daily from all hosts (df, SNMP). Ensure UsePct and filesystem/mount are extracted. Use Splunk `predict` with LLP5 for 30/60/90-day forecasting. Alert when projected usage exceeds 85% within 30 days or 95% within 90 days. Exclude ephemeral or tmpfs mounts from alerts. Build a dashboard with forecast overlay and drilldown to host/filesystem.
visualization: Timechart (usage with forecast overlay), Table (volumes approaching exhaustion with risk status), Gauge (current utilization), Single value (volumes at risk).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Planned change activity in the CMDB or change calendar produces expected deviations that match this detection pattern during approved maintenance. Cross-check ServiceNow change records for `state=implement` and the affected CI list.

2. **Backup and batch job cycles** — Nightly ETL, backup agents, or log rotation jobs generate bursts of similar events that resemble alert conditions but occur on a fixed schedule. Compare `_time` against the documented batch window before paging.

3. **Onboarding and provisioning bursts** — New users, devices, or services provisioned in bulk can temporarily skew counts until baselines stabilize. Filter events tagged `onboarding=true` in the identity or asset lookup.

4. **Monitoring and health-check traffic** — Synthetic transactions or internal scanner accounts generate probe traffic designed to exercise the control. Exclude service accounts listed in `monitoring_exceptions.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain a KV Store lookup `operational_exceptions.csv` with columns `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `approved_by`. Join the saved search to this lookup and filter `where isnull(exception_reason) OR now() > valid_until` so approved windows suppress alerts without muting the search globally.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: `Splunk_TA_nix`, SNMP-based storage inputs.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: df/disk usage data (any sourcetype with UsePct and filesystem), SNMP storage MIBs.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect disk usage metrics daily from all hosts (df and SNMP). Ensure UsePct and filesystem/mount are extracted. Use Splunk `predict` with LLP5 for 30/60/90-day forecasting. Alert when projected usage exceeds 85% within 30 days or 95% within 90 days. Exclude ephemeral or tmpfs mounts from alerts. Build a dashboard with forecast overlay and drilldown to host/filesystem.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=infrastructure (sourcetype="df" OR sourcetype="disk")
| eval UsePct=coalesce(UsePct, pctUsed, 'Percent_Used')
| eval filesystem=coalesce(filesystem, mount, instance)
| where isnotnull(UsePct) AND isnotnull(filesystem)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats latest(UsePct) as used_pct by filesystem, host, _time
| timechart span=1d latest(used_pct) as used_pct by filesystem, host
| predict used_pct as predicted_pct algorithm=LLP5 future_timespan=90
| eval risk_30d=if('predicted_pct+30d'>85, "At Risk", "OK")
| eval risk_90d=if('predicted_pct+90d'>95, "Critical", "OK")
| where risk_30d="At Risk" OR risk_90d="Critical"
| table _time, filesystem, host, used_pct, 'predicted_pct+30d', 'predicted_pct+90d', risk_30d, risk_90d
```

Understanding this SPL

**Predictive Disk / Volume Exhaustion** — Time-to-full forecast using linear regression on disk usage data enables proactive capacity planning. Running out of disk space causes application outages, failed backups, and data loss. Predicting exhaustion dates allows teams to provision storage or archive data before hitting critical thresholds.

Documented **Data sources**: df/disk usage data (any sourcetype with UsePct and filesystem), SNMP storage MIBs. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): `Splunk_TA_nix`, SNMP-based storage inputs. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: infrastructure; **sourcetype**: df, disk. Those sourcetypes align with what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=infrastructure, sourcetype="df". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **UsePct** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **filesystem** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Filters the current rows with `where isnotnull(UsePct) AND isnotnull(filesystem)` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• Discretizes time or numeric ranges with `bin`/`bucket`.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by filesystem, host, _time** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `timechart` plots the metric over time using **span=1d** buckets with a separate series **by filesystem, host** — ideal for trending and alerting on this use case.
• Pipeline stage (see **Predictive Disk / Volume Exhaustion**): predict used_pct as predicted_pct algorithm=LLP5 future_timespan=90
• `eval` defines or adjusts **risk_30d** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **risk_90d** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Filters the current rows with `where risk_30d="At Risk" OR risk_90d="Critical"` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• Pipeline stage (see **Predictive Disk / Volume Exhaustion**): table _time, filesystem, host, used_pct, 'predicted_pct+30d', 'predicted_pct+90d', risk_30d, risk_90d

compare with vROps capacity dashboard; compare with the cloud billing console for the same scope, accounts, and time range.

Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner.
